extracted.intended_audience: researchers and practitioners in autoformalization/formal theorem proving; developers replicating experiments or contributing to the ProofNet dataset
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for using, replicating, and contributing to the ProofNet benchmark for autoformalization and formal proving of undergraduate-level mathematics. Covers expected dataset item format, repository layout, scripts for evaluation and training, and contribution steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Example composition (per-example format)
rubrics_metrics.description: ProofNet benchmarks consists of 371 examples, each consisting of a formal theorem statement in Lean 3, a natural language theorem statement, and a natural language proof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each dataset item must include three parallel artifacts: (1) a Lean 3 formal theorem statement, (2) a corresponding natural-language theorem statement, and (3) a corresponding natural-language proof. The dataset size is 371 examples (as provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Domain coverage / topical scope
rubrics_metrics.description: The problems are primarily drawn from popular undergraduate pure mathematics textbooks and cover topics such as real and complex analysis, linear algebra, abstract algebra, and topology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When adding or evaluating items, ensure they are within undergraduate-level pure mathematics and fit the topical coverage (analysis, linear algebra, abstract algebra, topology, etc.), reflecting the dataset's intended domain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intended difficulty and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: ProofNet is a benchmark for autoformalization and formal proving of undergraduate-level mathematics; we intend for ProofNet to be a challenging benchmark that will drive progress in autoformalization and automatic theorem proving.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the benchmark to evaluate systems on challenging undergraduate-level problems; items should present nontrivial undergraduate proofs suitable to stress autoformalization and ATP systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repository use and replication guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: This repo is intended for replicating experimental results and accepting PRs to the dataset. To use ProofNet for your own experiments, use the Huggingface dataset.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For experiments prefer the Huggingface-hosted dataset distribution. The repository contains code and scripts (eval, calc_perplexity, train_backtranslation) to replicate experiments from the paper; follow those scripts for evaluation and replication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contribution workflow / dataset maintenance
rubrics_metrics.description: If you wish to open a PR for the dataset, modify the Lean and TeX source in benchmark/benchmark_to_publish and run parse_files.py.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dataset edits should be made to the .lean and TeX source files in benchmark/benchmark_to_publish. After changes, run parse_files.py to regenerate the published dataset artifacts before opening a PR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Directory / script purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: Directory Structure: benchmark/ contains .lean and TeX source files for maintaining the dataset. calc_perplexity contains scripts for calculating proof-pile and arXiv perplexity. eval contains scripts for running the autoformalization and informalization experiments found in the paper. train_backtranslation contains code for extracting mathlib declarations, informalizing mathlib using the OpenAI API, and fine-tuning distilled backtranslation models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the indicated directories for their described tasks: maintain dataset sources in benchmark/, compute perplexities with calc_perplexity scripts, run reproduction experiments via eval/, and use train_backtranslation/ for data-augmentation and model fine-tuning workflows. Follow the scripts' README/comments for parameters and runtime details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lean version compatibility notice
rubrics_metrics.description: Warning: This repository hosts the original Lean 3 version of ProofNet. Since Lean 3 is no longer maintained, you should use one of the Lean 4 ports of ProofNet, such as the one contained in deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-Prover-V1.5.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer Lean 4 ports for new experiments. If working with this repository, be aware of Lean 3's maintenance status and the availability of Lean 4 ports (which may be better supported).

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation / attribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Citation provided: ProofNet: Autoformalizing and Formally Proving Undergraduate-Level Mathematics (azerbayev2023proofnet, arXiv:2302.12433).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using or publishing results based on ProofNet, cite the provided paper/preprint and authors as given in the repository's citation block.
